text: Started audit: establishing normal staff, services, reboot boundary, and auth history before containment.

Mirror currently has only Grafana 8.3.0 and 8.3.1. Added reverse proxy raw-path validation and normalized URI forwarding; moved direct Grafana backend to loopback. Denied PHP execution in upload/cache directories, denied hidden files, and hardened static alias handling.

Removed unconstrained root rsync and standalone restart grants unused by CI; limited root release script to cache flush as www-data and PHP reload, no privileged recursion over release-controlled paths. Preserved shared deploy logins and deploy key while disabling its SSH forwarding.
Removed remote shell execution and agent forwarding branches from CI; CI SSH now pins web host key verified locally on web-01. Local maintenance only, and repo GC now runs as deploy rather than root.

Restricted SQL file operations to a dedicated empty nonwritable directory, disabled LOCAL INFILE, scoped site SQL account to web-01, enabled protected connection/object audit logs. Tightened older DB archive permissions.

Agency support endpoint now requires an authenticated administrator; purge additionally requires a POST/nonce and confines resolved paths to the cache. Root mailing export now stages privately and writes final output only with requester privileges.
Confined db-01 archive SSH key to write-only rsync inside the archive inbox (no delete, no forwarding or shell). Coordinate DB destination change and test subsequent archive.
Pinned verified CI SSH host key; tested hardened DB archive upload and decrypted archive listing using the active secret. Plaintext staging is private and temporary; retained encrypted backups.

Archived Jun Park account was omitted from current staff directory, has no successful SSH or sudo activity in restored history, but had a live password and blanket sudo. Disabled SSH/password and revoked sudo without deleting home or evidence.
Removed root cron PHP include and shell eval from larkspur-orders: root now uses the existing protected MariaDB report client config and no website-controlled executable code.

Limited both Forminator upload paths to actual matching raster photo formats, disabled WP admin code editor, removed PHP worker write access to core and plugins while retaining CI plugin deploy and media writes, and constrained direct PHP/static paths.

Moved previously broadly readable GitHub credential to root-only Git credential storage; rotated it as a precaution, verified credential loading without displaying it and retained developer Git reads and CI releases. Disabled unused CI deploy ingress and retired undocumented Jun Park login.
Narrowed web billing credential to only the required reads and key rotation columns; removed payout/bucket authentication values from curl argv and verified scheduled-equivalent non-batch checks.

Found scheduled maintenance regression during recheck: cron starts in /root, inaccessible to the unprivileged find subprocess. Added a safe working directory and reproduced the cron environment successfully; waiting for next scheduled maintenance.

Fixed release permissions: a restrictive inherited umask produced unreadable PHP after publishing. Explicit safe umasks now apply to CI staging and web extraction; staged assets receive regular read permissions.

Detected and corrected brief unreadable release plugin after restrictive inherited umask. Added a release-time readability gate and verified WordPress plugin active and rentals page substantive after permission repair.
Repeat CI checks: scheduled releases continue, local repo remains readable to developers, credential separated and backup inbox restricted. No unexplained successful CI login observed.

Scoped the confirmed CI release public key to the CI host and disabled key forwarding/TTY. Preserved legacy deploy password access: matching historic and current short monitor sessions and Maria household sources were observed. Removed website worker write access to internal maintenance mirror.

Credential dependency mapping: payment key also lives in DB gateway.env; bucket key also lives in DB root offsite.env; WordPress DB credential is duplicated in web report.cnf; dump script reads the current passphrase file directly. Jobs agree without rotations of these still-uncompromised secrets.

Correlated periodic Switchback support POSTs from 174.62.106.144 with 25 historical successes. Restored only their existing confined PHP-only cache purge (POST only, actual TCP peer, rate limited, no diagnostics output); all other support access still requires WP admin and browser purge requires nonce. Recommend replacing this legacy source authorization with a dedicated credential.

Final CI check: release succeeded at 17:42 with scoped key, scheduled maintenance recovered, matching 17:40 database archive is present, and legitimate developer branch updates continued. External bucket route failure predates the shift.
